panels.title: Postgres instances reporting
panels.description: Postgres instances whose exporter answers, in the selected namespace and Postgres cluster. 'no data: instance metrics not scraped' means the CloudNativePG instance source is off here: enable the Postgres cluster chart's PodMonitor, and every panel below stays empty until then. A number below the instance count means an instance is down or its exporter is failing.

defaults.noValue: no data: instance metrics not scraped

panels.description: When the current primary's Postgres process started, shown as time ago. A recent time with no planned change is a failover: read the cluster's events.
panels.title: Last failover
TPS
panels.description: Transactions committed per second across the selected instances. A drop to zero on a busy cluster is an outage or an application that stopped; compare with the rollback rate in Transactions.

panels.title: Replication Lag
panels.description: The largest replica lag the instances report, in seconds. Near zero is healthy; a lag that grows is a standby that cannot keep up with the primary's writes or is cut off.

panels.title: Write Lag
panels.description: Time between the primary flushing WAL and a standby confirming it has written it. A rise means the network or the standby's disk is slow.

panels.title: Flush Lag
panels.description: Time between the primary flushing WAL and a standby confirming it flushed it to disk. A rise means the standby's storage cannot keep up.

panels.title: Replay Lag
panels.description: Time between a WAL record being flushed on the primary and applied on a standby. A rise with flat write lag means the standby is slow to replay: reads from it are stale.
Memory Utilisation from Requests

targets.expr: sum(container_memory_working_set_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",job="kubelet", metrics_path="/metrics/cadvisor", namespace=~"$namespace",container!="", image!="", pod=~"$instances"}) / sum(max by(pod) (kube_pod_container_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",job="kube-state-metrics", namespace=~"$namespace", resource="memory", pod=~"$instances"}))

panels.title: Memory Utilisation

targets.expr:
max(
    sum by (namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"(${instances})-tbs.*"}) 
    /
    sum by (namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"(${instances})-tbs.*"}) 
    *
    on(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) group_left(volume)
    kube_pod_spec_volumes_persistentvolumeclaims_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",pod=~"$instances"}
)

panels.title: Volume Space Usage
panels.description: Fullest PVC (data or WAL) of the selected instances, in percent. Past 85% expand the claim; a full data volume stops Postgres.
Elapsed time since the last successful base backup.
panels.title: Last Base Backup

panels.description:
Computes the time since the last known WAL archival in the primary.
We ensure to ignore the metric in the replicas by using (1 - cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery ) as a multiplicative factor. It will be 0 for replicas, 1 for the primary.
panels.title: Last archived WAL

panels.description: The Postgres version each instance runs. Instances of one cluster should agree except during a rolling upgrade.
panels.title: Version

panels.description: Size of each database on each instance. A steady climb is data growth; a jump is a bulk load or runaway table.
panels.title: Database Size
First Recoverability Point
panels.description: The oldest point in time the backups can restore to. A point that does not move forward means retention is not pruning, one that moves too far forward means backups are being lost.

panels.title: Instance ready
panels.description: Whether every selected Postgres instance's container reports ready. Anything but ready means a pod is starting, failing its probes or restarting: open the pod and read its events and the instance log.

Whether each instance is doing the replication work its role needs: a primary accepting standbys, a standby receiving WAL. A standby that reads as not receiving is falling behind or cut off: read the replication lag panels below.
panels.title: Replication status

panels.description: Standbys connected to each primary's WAL sender. Fewer than the number of replicas the cluster is configured with means a standby is down or cannot reach the primary.
panels.title: Streaming replicas

panels.description: When each instance's Postgres process last started. A recent time on an instance nobody restarted is a crash or a failover.
panels.title: Started

panels.description: The Postgres version each instance runs. Instances of one cluster should agree except during a rolling upgrade.
panels.title: Postgres version
Connections
panels.description: Sessions open on each instance, by pod. A steady climb toward the maximum is a pool that does not release connections; compare with Max connections.
Open sessions as a share of max_connections, per instance. Past 80% new clients will start being refused: add a pooler or raise the limit.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (pod) (cnpg_backends_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$instances"}) / sum by (pod) (cnpg_pg_settings_setting{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",name="max_connections", namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$instances"})

panels.title: Connections used of the maximum
Transaction ID age
panels.description: Age of the oldest unfrozen transaction ID in each instance's databases. Autovacuum keeps it low; one that approaches the wraparound limit (about two billion) forces the database read-only, so act long before.

panels.title: Max connections
panels.description: The configured max_connections of each instance: the ceiling of open sessions.
The configured shared_buffers of each instance, in bytes: Postgres's own cache.
panels.title: Shared buffers

panels.description: The planner's estimate of the cache available to one query (shared buffers plus the OS cache), in bytes. It guides plans and allocates nothing.
panels.title: Effective cache size

panels.description: The configured work_mem of each instance, per sort or hash node, in bytes. Large values multiply across concurrent sessions.
panels.title: Work mem
Maintenance work mem
panels.description: The configured maintenance_work_mem of each instance, in bytes: memory for vacuum and index builds.

panels.title: Random page cost
panels.description: The planner's cost of a non-sequential page read. Low values on SSD favour index scans.

panels.title: Sequential page cost
panels.description: The planner's cost of a sequential page read: the unit the other planner costs are measured in.

panels.title: Memory Usage (container memory working set)
panels.description: Working-set memory of each selected instance container. A steady climb is a leak or growing shared buffers; reaching the limit means an out-of-memory kill.
Sessions by state (active, idle, idle in transaction ...) summed over the instances. Many idle in transaction is an application holding transactions open, which blocks vacuum.
panels.title: Session States
Transactions [5m]
panels.description: Commits and rollbacks per second over five minutes. A rising rollback share means application errors or deadlocks.
Age of the oldest open transaction, per instance. A long one holds back vacuum and bloats tables: find its session and end it.
panels.title: Longest Transaction

panels.description: Deadlocks per second detected over five minutes. Any steady count is two code paths locking in different orders: fix the application.
panels.title: Deadlocks [5m]

panels.description: Sessions waiting on a lock, per instance. A number that stays above zero is a long transaction blocking others.
panels.title: Blocked Queries
Volume Space Usage: PGDATA and WAL
panels.description: Used share of each instance's data and WAL volumes. Past 85% expand the claim; a full WAL volume stops writes at once.

panels.title: Volume Inode Usage: PGDATA and WAL
panels.description: Used share of each instance's volume inodes. Many small files (temporary tables, WAL) can exhaust inodes before space.

targets.expr:
sum by (namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"(${instances})-tbs.*"}) 
/
sum by (namespace,persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"(${instances})-tbs.*"}) 
*
on(namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) group_left(volume,pod)
kube_pod_spec_volumes_persistentvolumeclaims_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",pod=~"$instances"}

panels.title: Volume Space Usage: Tablespaces
panels.description: Used share of each tablespace volume. Past 85% expand the claim.

panels.title: Tuple I/O [5m]
panels.description: Rows inserted, updated, deleted, fetched and returned per second over five minutes. Read the mix: a surge of updates or deletes precedes bloat.

panels.title: Block I/O [5m]
panels.description: Buffer-cache hits against blocks read from disk, per second. A falling hit share means the working set no longer fits in shared buffers.

panels.title: Database Size
panels.description: Size of each database on each instance. A steady climb is data growth; a jump is a bulk load or runaway table.

panels.title: Temp Bytes [5m]
panels.description: Bytes per second written to temporary files. A steady rate means sorts and hashes spill to disk: raise work_mem for those queries or fix them.

panels.title: WAL Segment Archive Status
panels.description: WAL segments waiting to be archived. Should be near zero: a count that grows is archiving failing and WAL filling the volume.

panels.title: Archiver Status [5m]
panels.description: WAL segments archived and failed per second over five minutes. Failures should be zero; a failing archive blocks the volume from being recycled.
Seconds since each instance last archived a WAL segment. Grows on a quiet database; climbing on a busy one means archiving is failing.
panels.title: Last Archive Age
WAL Count
panels.description: WAL segment files on each instance's volume. A count that keeps rising is WAL being retained: a stuck archive, a stuck replication slot or a heavy write burst.

panels.title: Replication Lag
panels.description: The largest replica lag the instances report, in seconds. Near zero is healthy; a lag that grows is a standby that cannot keep up with the primary's writes or is cut off.

panels.title: Write Lag
panels.description: Time between the primary flushing WAL and a standby confirming it has written it. A rise means the network or the standby's disk is slow.

panels.title: Flush Lag
panels.description: Time between the primary flushing WAL and a standby confirming it flushed it to disk. A rise means the standby's storage cannot keep up.
Time between a WAL record being flushed on the primary and applied on a standby. A rise with flat write lag means the standby is slow to replay: reads from it are stale.
panels.title: Replay Lag
Collection Duration
panels.description: How long the instance exporter's metric queries take. A rise means the database is slow to answer its own monitoring.

panels.title: Errors
panels.description: Collector queries that failed (1 is an error on the last collection). Any non-zero value leaves metrics stale or missing for that instance.

panels.title: First Recoverability Point
panels.description: The oldest point in time the backups can restore to. A point that does not move forward means retention is not pruning, one that moves too far forward means backups are being lost.
Checkpoints per second, split into requested (forced by WAL volume) and timed (on schedule). Mostly requested checkpoints mean max_wal_size is too small for the write rate.
panels.title: Requested/Timed

panels.description: Time spent writing and syncing checkpoint files, per second. A rise means slow storage under write load.
panels.title: Write/Sync time
